claim_annotations.claim_text: The client agreed to provide weekly rides despite wanting to preserve Sunday mornings for rest.

evidence.evidence_text: I said yes, even though I had planned to use Sunday mornings to rest.
evidence.speaker: Client

evidence.evidence_text: My mother called on Sunday and asked me to drive her to appointments every week.
evidence.speaker: Client

claim_annotations.assessment_rationale: The client explicitly describes the request, agreement, and pre-existing plan to rest.

claim_annotations.claim_text: A previous critical comment from the mother may contribute to the client’s expectation of criticism.

evidence.evidence_text: When I imagine saying no, I feel guilty and think she will say I am selfish.
evidence.speaker: Client

evidence.evidence_text: She said it once last winter when I could not take her to a store.
evidence.speaker: Client

claim_annotations.assessment_rationale: The client reports both expecting the same criticism and hearing it once before, which is consistent with the hypothesis but does not establish that the prior comment caused the expectation.

claim_annotations.claim_text: Agreeing without discussing limits may be a way to avoid the discomfort of anticipated criticism.

evidence.evidence_text: When I imagine saying no, I feel guilty and think she will say I am selfish.
evidence.speaker: Client

evidence.evidence_text: I have not told her I want to change the plan.
evidence.speaker: Client

claim_annotations.assessment_rationale: The reported guilt, anticipated criticism, and unexpressed wish to change the arrangement support this as a possibility, but the client does not explicitly identify avoidance as the reason for agreeing.

claim_annotations.claim_text: The client has no dependable support outside the relationship with the mother and is managing the appointments alone.

evidence.evidence_text: My brother offered to take one of the appointments next week, and I felt relieved when he offered.
evidence.speaker: Client

claim_annotations.assessment_rationale: The client explicitly reports that a brother offered practical help, contradicting the claim that there is no dependable support and that the client is managing alone.

model_formulation: The client agreed to provide weekly rides despite wanting to preserve Sunday mornings for rest, and reports guilt and concern about being called selfish when considering a refusal. A previous critical comment from the mother may contribute to the client’s expectation of criticism, and agreeing without discussing limits may be a way to avoid that discomfort. The client has no dependable support outside the relationship with the mother and is managing the appointments alone.
session_transcript:
T1 Client: My mother called on Sunday and asked me to drive her to appointments every week.
T2 Therapist: How did you respond?
T3 Client: I said yes, even though I had planned to use Sunday mornings to rest.
T4 Client: When I imagine saying no, I feel guilty and think she will say I am selfish.
T5 Therapist: Has she said that to you before?
T6 Client: She said it once last winter when I could not take her to a store.
T7 Therapist: What has the arrangement been like since you agreed?
T8 Client: I have driven her twice so far. I was tired afterward, but I have not told her I want to change the plan.
T9 Therapist: Is there anyone else you can lean on?
T10 Client: My brother offered to take one of the appointments next week, and I felt relieved when he offered.
